HOW TO PLAY 2

Brick Break 2 flips the first game upside down. Two big changes run everything here: the ball starts at the top of the screen — not on your paddle — and hitting a brick scores nothing by itself. The points only count when you catch the falling brick. Read this page and you're playing a different game from Brick Break 1.

THE DROP

Every serve, your ball waits at the top of the playfield, above the brick wall. A solid wall runs under the coin bank at the very top of the screen — the ball bounces off it, so it can never slip up behind the coins. And a glowing floor line runs across the upper field: the ball bounces off that too, so the ball lives up top and NEVER comes down to your paddle. Tap anywhere on the screen to launch and it dives onto the bricks, bouncing around the top of the screen and smashing bricks loose. Your paddle never touches the ball at all — its only job is catching the bricks that rain down past the line. Each new level speeds up slightly — the ball and the falling bricks move just a little faster every level, all the way to Level 100, so the game keeps getting quicker without ever jumping suddenly. The ball can't be lost: your 3 serves are only at risk in Progressive, where the drifting wall can reach your paddle line.

THE WALL

The bricks still stand side by side in neat, tight rows — but never in the same colour rows twice. The four kinds are shuffled and dealt into the wall at random every level, so green, maroon, black and yellow sit mixed together in a new pattern each time you play.

CATCH TO SCORE

When the ball smashes a brick, the brick explodes loose and falls — tumbling down with its own random speed, sway and spin, never the same fall twice. That's your moment: slide the paddle under it and catch it. The catch pays out the brick's points and banks a token of its colour in the bar at the top of the screen. Let it fall past you and the points are gone — a hit with no catch scores zero. Your tokens bank and roll over from level to level, and your final counts are shown on the Game Over screen.

Scoring (paid on the catch only): green XMΣMΣ bricks 7 PTS, maroon FARM bricks 5 PTS, black XRPMAN bricks 3 PTS, yellow CORN bricks 1 PT.

YOUR PADDLE'S ONE JOB: CATCHING

Your paddle is a basket, nothing else: the ball stays up top and never reaches it, so the paddle's whole game is getting under the falling bricks to haul in the points. It stays full size the whole game — it never shrinks. Move it with the mouse, touch-drag, or the ← → / A D keys. Pause with P.

Passing a level — catch enough bricks: knock every brick loose from the wall — caught or missed, a loose brick is off the wall — and catch the percentage your level asks for: 60% on Levels 1–30, 70% on Levels 31–60, 80% on Levels 61–90, and 85% on Levels 91–100. The CAUGHT counter at the top right of the screen shows your percentage and the % you need for this level as you play, and turns green once you reach it. Clear the wall but finish under your level's mark and the level does not count — it uses one of your 3 tries and you play the level over. Pass Level 100 and you beat the game.

Pick your ball: after Enter Game, choose one of the 12 characters below on the Home Screen. Every character plays the same — same speed, same bounce — only the look changes. The picture balls are round badges that roll as they bounce.

THE CHARACTERS

  • XRPMan: the hero ball — tiny superhero in his classic black suit with bright green #00ff00 highlights, one arm punched forward like Superman and little thruster flames firing from his boots as he flies. He always turns to face the way he's flying.
  • Farm Emblem: the Farmers Union badge ball — the farm emblem in a lime-green ring.
  • Mr. Scribbles: the artist ball — Mr. Scribbles' scribble-art badge in a silver-white ring.
  • Xolo: the Xolo ball — Xolo's badge in a bright green ring.
  • Maganon: the Maganon ball — Maganon's badge in a red ring.
  • BWIF: the BWIF ball — BWIF's badge in a tan ring.
  • XMΣMΣ: the XMΣMΣ ball — neon-green XMΣMΣ badge in a bright #00ff00 green ring.
  • SPEC: the SPEC ball — Spec's badge in a yellow ring.
  • Big Chief: the Big Chief ball — the pink duck with the brain on top and the big orange bill, in a hot-pink ring.
  • Spiffy: the Spiffy ball — the black-and-white line-drawing face with the cap, the beard and the rolled smoke, in a white ring.
  • Lenny: the Lenny ball — the blue Lenny face badge in a bright green ring.
  • XOGE: the XOGE ball — the red panda holding the X coin on its stand, in a rust-orange ring.

THE MODES

Classic — one paddle, one ball working the top of the screen. Knock the whole wall loose and catch what you can on the way down.

Cavity — two bricks in the wall hold a trapped ball inside. Knock one loose and its ball flies free to join the drop.

Progressive — the wall keeps drifting down while fresh bricks stack in on top, side by side. Knock them loose before one reaches your paddle line, or you lose a serve. Its wall never ends, so there's no pass mark there — the CAUGHT counter just tracks your running catch rate.

One ball only: you play with exactly 1 ball on every level, for the whole run — clearing levels never adds more. It starts at the top, stays up top bouncing off the floor line, and can never be lost past your paddle. (Cavity is the one exception: freeing a trapped ball there is that mode's own trick, not a bonus.)

Playing a level over: run out of serves on a level and you can play that level over — same level, fresh shuffled wall, 3 fresh serves, and your score back to what it was when the level started. You get 3 tries at each level. If you still haven't cleared it after the 3rd try, it's Game Over — tap HOME SCREEN to go back to the Home Screen and start again.
